name: Supply-chain security
description: Supply-chain-security playbook scaffold (NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555, Article 21(2)(d)). Detects and responds to supply-chain compromises that reach the operator through a direct supplier, service provider, or upstream software component. SKELETON: pins the workflow topology (workflow_start -> assess-supplier-signal -> emit-supply-chain-evidence -> workflow_end) and the x_secops_ng joins into the SecOps-NG content model; per-target compiler emitters (n8n / Temporal / LangGraph), regulatory-mapping fan-out (OSCAL / D3FEND / NIS2 / DORA / CRA inbound + outbound), metric refs, and byte-parity goldens are out of scope and land in CORE / EXTEND sibling cards. The shipped action bodies are placeholders that pin the contract only; real action logic is delegated to the CORE sibling card.

__execution_id__.description: Per-execution identifier issued by the compile target's workflow runtime (n8n execution id, Temporal workflow run id, LangGraph thread/checkpoint id). Pinned by the upstream runtime; the workflow reads it for the supply-chain-evidence artifact join.

__supplier_signal_ref__.description: Pointer to the inbound supply-chain signal under processing on this execution. Operator-configured; the workflow reads it as an opaque pointer to a signal record held in the operator's threat-intel surface, supplier-attestation feed, SBOM-watch tooling, or upstream-advisory inbox. The framework ships no default hosted feed dependency, no default non-EU endpoint, and no vendor SDK bundling — the operator supplies whatever signal source is in scope.

__assessment_ref__.description: Pointer to the supply-chain-impact assessment record produced by assess-supplier-signal. Closed shape per CORE sibling card; verdict-keyed (no_impact | watch | confirmed_compromise), affected-supplier-handle and affected-component-set valued. Consumed by emit-supply-chain-evidence.

__supply_chain_artifact_ref__.description: Pointer to the supply-chain-evidence artifact emitted by emit-supply-chain-evidence. Anchored against the F-CP-03 supply-chain evidence stream so the NIS2 Article 21(2)(d) supplier-security obligation has a per-execution audit-trail entry. Schema and emission target are operator-configured and detailed in the CORE / EXTEND sibling cards.

action--5c5c5c5c-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: assess-supplier-signal
action--5c5c5c5c-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Read the inbound supply-chain signal referenced by __supplier_signal_ref__ from the operator-supplied signal source and bind it to a normalised supply-chain-impact assessment record (verdict in {no_impact, watch, confirmed_compromise}, affected_supplier_handle, affected_component_set, received_at). SKELETON placeholder: this step pins the contract only — the actual assessment policy (signal-source ingestion, SBOM correlation, supplier-attestation lookup, verdict scoring) is delegated to the CORE primitive bound in the CORE sibling card. Read-only against the operator's signal source by contract; the workflow MUST NOT mutate the source signal on this step.

action--5c5c5c5c-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: emit-supply-chain-evidence
action--5c5c5c5c-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Combine the execution metadata and the supply-chain-impact assessment record into one supply-chain-evidence artifact anchored against the F-CP-03 supply-chain evidence stream, so the NIS2 Article 21(2)(d) supplier-security obligation has a per-execution audit-trail entry. SKELETON placeholder: the artifact shape (schema reference, classification flags, captured_at, provenance, regulation_refs) is pinned by the CORE / EXTEND sibling cards; this step pins the contract only. Destination is operator-configured — no default non-EU endpoint.
